current.text: Minnesota traded away Julius Randle and Naz Reid, signed Jonathan Kuminga and has a full season of Ayo Dosunmu. Donte DiVincenzo is out for most of the season.
He is a projected starter with Ball, Edwards and Gobert. Finch said he will play some power forward but probably will not start there or play all his minutes there.
Minnesota has very little frontcourt depth and may play small lineups with three guards, so rebounds and shots left by Reid and Randle get spread to the remaining players.
Experts expect his usage and output to rise this season with Reid and Randle gone. He gets a further usage spike if a teammate misses time.

The Kuminga signing hurts him a little because Kuminga will take shots. Experts disagree on how much: one doubts he reaches 20 percent usage, others say he keeps his starting spot and should still beat his price.
His market rank of about 90 to 98 is too late. The newest call is to take him in the 70s in category leagues.
In an expert auction mock draft he went for 11 USD as the buyer's first player.
With a March 28 end, Minnesota's playoff schedule goes 4, 2, 4 games, so the semifinal week (starting March 15) has only two games. The team has the league minimum of 13 back-to-backs.
Minnesota is expected to compete, with one expert predicting 53 wins, so late-season rest for tanking is unlikely.
Yahoo lists him as questionable for rest.

durable.text: He has a steals and blocks profile. He averaged a steal and a block a game over the final 20 games last season. Blocks are his strongest category for a forward, with good FG% for his position.
No category is weak in his projections, so he fits any build.
His usage has gone up in each of the last three seasons.
He is worth less in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: He costs little: average costs are 1.2 USD on Yahoo and 2.9 USD on ESPN, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. Experts would take him in the 70s, ahead of his Yahoo rank of 92 and ESPN rank of 81, so a bid up to his Yahoo value of 6 USD is fine. One mock buyer paid 11 USD. He fits any build as a source of blocks, steals and good FG% (51 percent on about 11 shots) with no weak category, but the two-game semifinal week lowers his playoff value. Early in the season, check whether his shots rise above last season's 11.1 per game with Kuminga around and how many minutes he plays at power forward.
